name: Grünfeld Defense
category: Hypermodern & Dynamic Asymmetric Defenses (1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 d5)
summary: Ernst Grünfeld's revolutionary hypermodern creation favored by Garry Kasparov, Bobby Fischer, and Peter Svidler. Black invites White to establish a massive d4/e4 pawn center, then ruthlessly dismantles it from afar with ...Bg7, ...c5, and ...Nc6.
keyConcepts: Conceding large center to attack it
Exchange on c3 & attacking d4/c3 base

subVariations.name: Grünfeld Exchange: Modern 8.Rb1 System
subVariations.description: The absolute pinnacle of modern Grünfeld theory. White activates the rook along the b-file with 8.Rb1, while Black targets the d5/c3 pawns with ...Bc7 and ...Ba5.
subVariations.whitePlan: Push f4 and d5 to advance passed pawns, attack down the b-file.
subVariations.blackPlan: Pin c3 with ...Ba5, blockade d5, apply pressure on White's pawn center.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld Exchange: Classical 7.Bc4
subVariations.description: The legendary battleground of the Kasparov-Karpov World Championship matches. White builds a massive center with Bc4 and Be3, while Black counterstrikes with ...Bg4 and ...Na5.
subVariations.whitePlan: Maintain dominating d4/e4 pawn center, launch kingside attack with f4-f5.
subVariations.blackPlan: Maneuver knight via Na5-c4, trade on d4, exploit the dark-square diagonals.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: Russian System (4.Nf3 Bg7 5.Qb3)
subVariations.description: Mikhail Botvinnik and Vasily Smyslov's weapon: 5.Qb3 forces 5...dxc4, regaining the pawn with the queen and building a central spatial grip.
subVariations.whitePlan: Maintain queen on b3/a3, use e5 space wedge, exploit Black's queenside pawns.
subVariations.blackPlan: Expand on queenside with ...a6 and ...b5, break with ...c5, target c5/e5 pawns.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: Russian System (5.Qa4+)
subVariations.description: White delivers a check on a4 to displace Black's bishop to d7 before recapturing on c4.
subVariations.whitePlan: Control center with Rd1 and e4, maintain queen safety on c4.
subVariations.blackPlan: Pin with ...Bg4, maneuver knight via Nfd7-b6, attack d4.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: 4.Bf4 Main Line
subVariations.description: High-voltage attacking system where White plays 4.Bf4 to target c7, met by an explosive ...d4 central counter-sacrifice by Black.
subVariations.whitePlan: Pressure c7 and d5, use active dark bishop on f4/g3.
subVariations.blackPlan: Advance ...d4! wedge, open lines for active minor pieces, exploit f3 weakening.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: 4.Bf4 with 4...c5 (Simagin)
subVariations.description: Tactical madness with multiple piece and rook sacrifices: Black wins a rook on a1 while White wins the rook on h8.
subVariations.whitePlan: Survive the queen checks, consolidate the material advantage.
subVariations.blackPlan: Attack White's exposed king on e2 with ...Be6 and ...Nc6, deliver mate.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: Fianchetto System (3.g3)
subVariations.description: Ultra-solid positional choice for White. By fianchettoing on g2, White blunts Black's g7 monster bishop.
subVariations.whitePlan: Control d5 outpost, clamp Black's pieces, grind in the endgame.
subVariations.blackPlan: Maneuver knight to a5/b6, break with ...c6 or ...e5, pressure d5.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: Modern 5.Bd2 System
subVariations.description: White plays 5.Bd2 to avoid doubled pawns on c3 and retain smooth piece development.
subVariations.whitePlan: Advance d5, utilize open g-file with Rg1, attack down the center.
subVariations.blackPlan: Trade on f3, anchor knight on a5/c4, pressure White's center.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: 4.Bg5 / Stockholm Variation
subVariations.description: White pins the knight with 4.Bg5, provoking 4...Ne4, followed by queenside pawn tension after 7.Qb1.
subVariations.whitePlan: Regain c4 with Bxc4, put pressure on b6, control center.
subVariations.blackPlan: Defend c4 pawn with ...Be6 and ...b6, coordinate smoothly.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: Flohr / 4.e3 System
subVariations.description: Salo Flohr's calm positional setup: White plays 4.e3, trading queens early into a strategic endgame.
subVariations.whitePlan: Exploit Black's doubled c-pawns, utilize bishop on c4.
subVariations.blackPlan: Maneuver knight to b6/d5, utilize open d-file and bishop pair.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: Prins Variation (5.Na4)
subVariations.description: Lodewijk Prins's knight move to a4, controlling c5 and preparing e4 dominance.
subVariations.whitePlan: Maintain central spatial advantage with d5/e4, use bishop pair.
subVariations.blackPlan: Anchor knight on e5, trade on a4, pressure White's queenside.

subVariations.name: Neo-Grünfeld: 3.f3 System (Alekhine)
subVariations.description: Alexander Alekhine's aggressive system: White reinforces e4 with f3 and castles long to launch an attack, while Black breaks with ...f5.
subVariations.whitePlan: Trade dark bishops with Bh6, push h4-h5, mate the black king.
subVariations.blackPlan: Counterstrike with ...f5 and ...Nb4, attack White's king on c1.

subVariations.name: Neo-Grünfeld: 3.g3 System
subVariations.description: White combines early g3/Bg2 with e4, establishing a solid d5 wedge.
subVariations.whitePlan: Maintain d5 pawn wedge, restrict Black's counterplay, expand on queenside.
subVariations.blackPlan: Undermine with ...e6 and ...c5, anchor knight on b4.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: Hungarian Variation (4.Nf3 Bg7 5.e3 O-O 6.Be2)
subVariations.description: Harmonious classical treatment leading to IQP structures where Black easily develops all minor pieces.
subVariations.whitePlan: Use active minor pieces on c4/e1, attack kingside.
subVariations.blackPlan: Fianchetto on b7, blockade d5 square, attack the d4 IQP.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: Burille Variation (4.cxd5 Nxd5 5.e4)
subVariations.description: Black delays ...Bg4 and develops the queen to c7, maintaining flexible pressure along the c- and d-files.
subVariations.whitePlan: Maintain d4/e4 pawn center, prepare f4 kingside attack.
subVariations.blackPlan: Pressure c-file with ...Qc7 and d-file with ...Rd8, undermine with ...e6.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: Seville Variation (7.Bc4 c5 8.Ne2 Nc6 9.Be3 O-O 10.O-O Bg4 11.f3 Na5 12.Bxf7+)
subVariations.description: Anatoly Karpov's dramatic bishop sacrifice on f7 against Garry Kasparov in the 1987 Seville World Championship Match.
subVariations.whitePlan: Maintain extra pawns, survive Black's centralized queen assault.
subVariations.blackPlan: Dominate central dark squares with ...Qd5, activate knight and bishop.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld Gambit (4.cxd5 c6)
subVariations.description: Black sacrifices a pawn with 4...c6 for open files and blazing piece activity.
subVariations.whitePlan: Consolidate extra pawn, trade queens, simplify into winning endgame.
subVariations.blackPlan: Create tactical threats with ...e4, dominate open b- and d-files.

subVariations.name: Grünfeld: 5.e3 Classical Setup
subVariations.description: White plays b4 to clamp the queenside and avoids sharp theoretical main lines.
subVariations.whitePlan: Expand on queenside with b4/a4, maintain bishop pair on d3/b2.
subVariations.blackPlan: Trade on f3, coordinate with ...Nbd7 and ...e6, break with ...e5.
